subject: primitive types in auto-dif: three options

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: primitive types in auto-dif: three options
parts:
I want to outline three options for dealing with primitive
arithmetic types (only double and int in Stan) in our functions.
This is related to the bug I just closed that was preventing
int arguments to matrix ops (they were getting cast to stan::agrad::var
instead of double due to argument-dependent lookup of the other
arg, which was a stan::agrad::var).

Proposal 1: Brute force expansion, no templates

template <int R, int C>
inline Eigen::Matrix<double,R,C>
multiply(const Eigen::Matrix<double,R,C>& m,
double c) {
return c * m;
}
template <int R, int C>
inline Eigen::Matrix<double,R,C>
multiply(const Eigen::Matrix<double,R,C>& m,
int c) {
return c * m;
}

Proposal 2: Explicit use of boost::enable_if

template <int R, int C, typename T>
inline Eigen::Matrix<double,R,C>
multiply(const Eigen::Matrix<typename boost::enable_if_c<boost::is_arithmetic<T>::value,
double>::type,
R, C>& m,
T c) {
return c * m;
}


Proposal 3: no-op encapsulation of enable_if

template <typename T>
inline void
validate_is_arithmetic(const typename boost::enable_if_c<boost::is_arithmetic<T>::value,
T>::type& /*v*/) {
/* no op helper function */
}

template <int R, int C, typename T>
inline
Eigen::Matrix<double,R,C>
multiply(const Eigen::Matrix<double,R,C>& m,
T c) {
validate_is_arithmetic<T>(0);
return c * m;
}


The problem with (1) is the additional code and that it's not
general for types other than int and double (and see below about
return).

The problem with (2) is that it's hard to type and to read.

The problem with (3) is that we need to lean on the compiler to
compile away the no-op function. (The argument 0 could also be c here.

To truly generalize our types to allow float returns, what we'd need is

template <int R, int C, typename T1, typename T2>
inline
Eigen::Matrix<typename boost::math::tools::promote_args<T1,T2>::type, R, C>
multiply(const Eigen::Matrix<T1, R, C>& m,
T2 c) {
validate_is_arithmetic<T1>(0);
validate_is_arithmetic<T2>(0);
return c * m;
}

Now there's not a good value to pass in for T1 (the matrix could be 0 x 0),
so it really has to be 0.

Given that reverse mode auto-diff is double only and we don't foresee
ever using float scalars or int matrices, I think we can get away with the
simpler version in proposal 3.

- Bob

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] primitive types in auto-dif: three options
parts:
The one advantage that option 2 has over option 3 is that option 2
could significantly reduce the amount of duplicated code we have
hanging around for mixed type operations. In other words, instead of
having three versions of a function, e.g.,

var dot_product(var, var)
var dot_product(var, double)
var dot_product(double, var)

we could have one

enable_if< is_same<var,T1>::value || is_same<var,T2>::value, var>
dot_product(T1,T2)

Cheers,
Marcus
